tasks.title: Setup grants, password verification, throttling and cookies enforce their lifetimes
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console — new setup-code, auth-throttle, passwords and cookies modules with their tests; Required behavior / console: setup code and setup grant, Sign-in hash parameters and dummy verification, the whole Throttle algorithm, and Cookies including refresh serialization. Keep these reusable authentication primitives independent of routes; inject clock, randomness and KDF functions, wire real ones only in main.ts later, and use real Bun.password in tests. Counterexamples / Setup code, Grant, Password, Throttle capacity and Throttle lock apply. Implement admission, reservations, settlement, cleanup and eviction as one limiter algorithm: reserve both entries atomically in one synchronous step, release the same reservations on failure/success/error, never remove locked or in-flight entries, and refuse capacity pressure without creating an entry or reservation in either table. Capacity refusals use the specified Retry-After calculation; HTTP logging/metrics follow in T4/T5. HTTP statuses, peer client-key selection, session refresh triggers and startup stdout are integrated in T4/T5, rather than splitting the limiter algorithm or KDF policy into separate tasks.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; all new module tests pass with 0 failures, full-suite line coverage >= 80% and cognitive complexity <= 15. A code uses 16 random bytes and matches [0-9a-f]{4}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){7}; normalization removes ASCII spaces/hyphens and lowercases before a timing-safe digest comparison. Only code/grant digests are retained; grants use 32 random bytes, expire after 1800000 ms, and replacement/completion/restart invalidate prior grants. Empty code is not counted. Password policy accepts 12 emoji and leading spaces, rejects 11 or 129 code points and unequal confirmation; real hashes start with $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$ and the dummy verifier uses the same costs. Both limiter tables admit at most 5 live/in-flight attempts, the fifth failure locks for 900000 ms from that failure, blocked attempts do not extend it, success clears only the account key, and expiry is exclusive at now-900000. Test the default 10000-key bounds, separate setup limiter and restart reset. Reservations settle on success, failure and request-ending error; cleanup and eviction never remove an entry with inFlight > 0, and locked entries have inFlight=0. Admission across both tables has no await and either reserves both entries or neither. Capacity refusal runs 0 verifications and counts 0 failures; its deterministic saturation, atomic-refusal and eviction cases are checked below. Literal cookie strings have Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict, no Domain, Secure and __Host- only in strict-https; session Max-Age=2592000, setup=1800, anonymous CSRF has no Max-Age, deletion=0 and refresh preserves the value.

All limiter cases pass, 0 fail; exercise the Throttle capacity counterexamples with the default 10000-key bound, an injected clock, explicit admissions/settlements and no KDF or real waits. At t=0 create 9999 locked account/client pairs; at t=1000 admit 4 unsettled owner@example.com/client-v attempts. At t=2000 a new@example.com/client-n attempt is refused with 429 and Retry-After=1, both tables stay at 10000 entries, both owner/v reservations remain inFlight=4, and neither new key exists. Settle the 4 failures at t=3000; at t=4000 admit exactly 1 more owner/v attempt and refuse a second pending one with 429 and Retry-After=1: exactly 5 owner admissions in this window, never 9. With 10000 locked pairs at t=0, a fresh key at t=1000 gets 429 and Retry-After=899, and at t=900000 is admitted. With the account table full of locked entries and the client table holding exactly 1 entry, refusal leaves exactly 1 client entry and adds 0 reservations. With 9999 locked pairs plus old@example.com/client-o holding 2 live failures and inFlight=0, a fresh pair evicts the old pair and is admitted; with 1 pending old/o attempt it gets 429 and Retry-After=1 and preserves that reservation. Idle cleanup removes only entries without live failures, live locks or pending attempts; otherwise eviction chooses the unlocked, zero-inFlight entry with the oldest last failure. Focused coverage may fail its threshold despite passing cases; the full-suite coverage gate is the separate bun run check acceptance.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; every console test passes, full-suite line coverage >= 80% and cognitive complexity <= 15. Wrong and unknown accounts return byte-identical 401 pages except CSRF; both execute real-cost verification and log no email/password. Empty fields/over-128-code-point passwords return 422 without counting. Five wrong passwords yield 5 x 401, the sixth including correct credentials yields 429 Retry-After: 900; at t5+899999 it stays 429, at t5+900000 correct credentials yield 303. Ten concurrent attempts give exactly 5 x 401 and 5 x 429. Account/client locks work separately, spoofed forwarding headers do not change the peer key, success clears only account failures, and the sliding-window counterexample does not lock. Successful sign-in rotates/revokes any old session, prunes expired rows and follows only valid next paths. Fabricated/revoked/expired sessions cannot access GET /. Idle +2591999999 ms is valid, +2592000000 expires; +59999 sends no session Set-Cookie, +60000 refreshes it. At day 29 (+2505600000) GET / is 200 with the same cookie and Max-Age=2592000; day 31 (+2678400000) remains 200. Sessions survive a new server on the same file. Sign-out with the session CSRF deletes the row, clears the cookie and returns 303 /sign-in; the anonymous token fails 403, and no-session sign-out changes nothing. All route/method/phase, cookie, next, CSP, POST-order, metrics and log cases match their spec literals.

Against bun start with a temporary database and local fake/dev API, perform and record the actual follow-up agent-browser commands of Acceptance evidence 7: direct setup without code is refused, unlock with stdout code, observe connection result, complete setup, sign in, sign out, reject a wrong password, sign in correctly and refuse the old code.
